```{r}
library(phyloseq)
setwd("C:/Users/DA.5015582/OneDrive - UAM/TRABAJO/Abiertos/Learning/ASV_vs_weight/")
ps <- readRDS("ps_nocontrol_filtrado_rare.rds")
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# STEP 1 — ASV screening for plant dry weight association analysis
#
# Description:
# This chunk extracts ASV relative abundances and plant dry weight
# (Peso_Seco) from the phyloseq object and computes summary statistics
# for each ASV across all samples.
#
# The goal is to identify ASVs with sufficient abundance and prevalence
# to be included in downstream correlation analyses with plant dry weight.
#
# Output:
# - Summary table with prevalence and abundance statistics for each ASV
# ============================================================

library(phyloseq)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

## Extract OTU table
otu_mat <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")

if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) {
  otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)
}

## Convert to relative abundance
rel_abund <- sweep(otu_mat, 1, rowSums(otu_mat), "/")

## Convert to long format
asv_long_weight <- as.data.frame(rel_abund) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("SampleID") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -SampleID,
    names_to = "ASV",
    values_to = "rel_abundance"
  )

## Add dry weight
sample_metadata <- data.frame(sample_data(ps)) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("SampleID") %>%
  select(SampleID, Peso_Seco, Componentes)

asv_long_weight <- asv_long_weight %>%
  left_join(sample_metadata, by = "SampleID")

## ASV summary stats
asv_weight_summary <- asv_long_weight %>%
  group_by(ASV) %>%
  summarise(
    n_present = sum(rel_abundance > 0),
    n_above_0.1pct = sum(rel_abundance >= 0.001),
    n_above_1pct = sum(rel_abundance >= 0.01),
    mean_abundance = mean(rel_abundance),
    median_abundance = median(rel_abundance),
    max_abundance = max(rel_abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_above_1pct))

print(asv_weight_summary, n = 30)

summary(asv_weight_summary$n_above_1pct)

# Saved objects:
# asv_long_weight   -> long-format ASV abundance + plant dry weight table
# asv_weight_summary -> ASV prevalence/abundance summary for filtering
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# STEP 2A — Compare ASV abundance/prevalence filters
#
# Description:
# This chunk compares relaxed and strict ASV filters for downstream
# association analyses with plant dry weight.
#
# Relaxed filter: ASV reaches >=0.1% relative abundance in at least 5 samples.
# Strict filter:  ASV reaches >=1% relative abundance in at least 5 samples.
#
# Output:
# - Number of retained ASVs under each filter
# - Candidate ASV vectors for relaxed and strict analyses
# ============================================================

candidate_asvs_relaxed <- asv_weight_summary %>%
  filter(n_above_0.1pct >= 5) %>%
  pull(ASV)

candidate_asvs_strict <- asv_weight_summary %>%
  filter(n_above_1pct >= 5) %>%
  pull(ASV)

cat("Relaxed filter: >=0.1% in >=5 samples\n")
cat("Number of ASVs:", length(candidate_asvs_relaxed), "\n\n")

cat("Strict filter: >=1% in >=5 samples\n")
cat("Number of ASVs:", length(candidate_asvs_strict), "\n\n")

cat("Strict ASVs included within relaxed set:",
    all(candidate_asvs_strict %in% candidate_asvs_relaxed), "\n")

# Saved objects:
# candidate_asvs_relaxed -> ASVs reaching >=0.1% in >=5 samples
# candidate_asvs_strict  -> ASVs reaching >=1% in >=5 samples
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# STEP 3 — Define ASV source sets and eligible samples
#
# Description:
# This chunk defines, for each ASV, its source set based on single-inoculum
# communities. An ASV is considered part of a single inoculum if its mean
# relative abundance across replicates of that single is >= 0.1%.
#
# Then, for each ASV, all eligible samples are identified as samples whose
# inoculum combination contains at least one source component.
#
# Finally, ASV prevalence is quantified across eligible samples to build
# an eligibility-aware filter for downstream dry-weight association analyses.
#
# Output:
# - ASV eligibility summary table
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Mean abundance of each ASV in single inocula
## ------------------------------------------------------------

single_asv_means <- asv_long_weight %>%
  filter(nchar(Componentes) == 1) %>%
  group_by(ASV, Componentes) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_single_abundance = mean(rel_abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Define source set
## ------------------------------------------------------------

asv_source_sets <- single_asv_means %>%
  filter(mean_single_abundance >= 0.001) %>%
  group_by(ASV) %>%
  summarise(
    source_components = list(Componentes),
    n_source_singles = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Get all samples
## ------------------------------------------------------------

sample_info <- asv_long_weight %>%
  select(SampleID, Componentes) %>%
  distinct()

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Compute eligibility metrics for each ASV
## ------------------------------------------------------------

asv_eligibility_summary <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(asv_source_sets)), function(i) {
  
  asv_i <- asv_source_sets$ASV[i]
  source_set <- unlist(asv_source_sets$source_components[[i]])
  
  eligible_samples <- sample_info %>%
    filter(
      sapply(Componentes, function(x) {
        any(str_detect(x, source_set))
      })
    )
  
  asv_data <- asv_long_weight %>%
    filter(
      ASV == asv_i,
      SampleID %in% eligible_samples$SampleID
    )
  
  tibble(
    ASV = asv_i,
    n_source_singles = length(source_set),
    n_eligible = nrow(eligible_samples),
    n_above_0.1pct_in_eligible = sum(asv_data$rel_abundance >= 0.001),
    prop_above_0.1pct_in_eligible =
      sum(asv_data$rel_abundance >= 0.001) / nrow(eligible_samples)
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Sort summary
## ------------------------------------------------------------

asv_eligibility_summary <- asv_eligibility_summary %>%
  arrange(desc(prop_above_0.1pct_in_eligible))

print(asv_eligibility_summary, n = 30)

summary(asv_eligibility_summary$prop_above_0.1pct_in_eligible)

# Saved objects:
# asv_source_sets -> source single inocula for each ASV
# asv_eligibility_summary -> eligibility-aware prevalence summary
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# STEP 4 — Generate ASV IDs and candidate ASV annotation table
#
# Description:
# This chunk creates simplified ASV identifiers (ASV_1, ASV_2, etc.)
# ranked by global mean relative abundance across all samples.
#
# Taxonomic annotation is extracted directly from the phyloseq object.
# Then, candidate ASVs passing the eligibility-aware filter are annotated
# with ASV IDs and taxonomy for downstream interpretation.
#
# Output:
# - Annotated candidate ASV table (IDs + taxonomy + eligibility metrics)
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Create ASV IDs ranked by global mean abundance
## ------------------------------------------------------------

asv_ids <- asv_long_weight %>%
  group_by(ASV) %>%
  summarise(global_abundance = sum(rel_abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(global_abundance)) %>%
  mutate(ASV_ID = paste0("ASV_", row_number())) %>%
  select(ASV, ASV_ID)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Extract taxonomy from phyloseq
## ------------------------------------------------------------

tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("ASV")

## Keep useful taxonomic levels if present
tax_cols <- intersect(
  c("Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus"),
  colnames(tax_df)
)

tax_df <- tax_df %>%
  select(ASV, all_of(tax_cols))

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Filter candidate ASVs
## ------------------------------------------------------------

candidate_asvs <- asv_eligibility_summary %>%
  filter(prop_above_0.1pct_in_eligible >= 0.1)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Annotate candidate ASVs
## ------------------------------------------------------------

candidate_asv_table <- candidate_asvs %>%
  left_join(asv_ids, by = "ASV") %>%
  left_join(tax_df, by = "ASV") %>%
  arrange(desc(prop_above_0.1pct_in_eligible))

print(candidate_asv_table, n = 30)

# Saved objects:
# asv_ids -> maps full ASV sequences to simplified ASV IDs
# tax_df -> taxonomic annotation extracted from phyloseq
# candidate_asv_table -> filtered candidate ASVs with IDs and taxonomy
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# STEP 5 — Eligibility-aware Spearman correlation with plant dry weight
#
# Description:
# This chunk tests whether each candidate ASV is monotonically associated
# with plant dry weight (Peso_Seco).
#
# For each ASV, only eligible samples are used. A sample is eligible when
# its inoculum combination contains at least one source component where
# that ASV was detected in single-inoculum communities.
#
# Spearman correlation is calculated between ASV relative abundance and
# Peso_Seco. P-values are corrected using Benjamini-Hochberg FDR.
#
# Output:
# - Spearman correlation table for candidate ASVs
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

candidate_asv_ids <- candidate_asv_table$ASV

asv_spearman_eligible <- lapply(candidate_asv_ids, function(asv_i) {

  source_set <- asv_source_sets %>%
    filter(ASV == asv_i) %>%
    pull(source_components) %>%
    .[[1]]

  eligible_samples <- sample_info %>%
    filter(
      sapply(Componentes, function(x) {
        any(str_detect(x, source_set))
      })
    )

  dat_i <- asv_long_weight %>%
    filter(
      ASV == asv_i,
      SampleID %in% eligible_samples$SampleID,
      !is.na(Peso_Seco)
    )

  test_i <- suppressWarnings(
    cor.test(
      dat_i$rel_abundance,
      dat_i$Peso_Seco,
      method = "spearman",
      exact = FALSE
    )
  )

  tibble(
    ASV = asv_i,
    n = nrow(dat_i),
    rho = unname(test_i$estimate),
    p_value = test_i$p.value
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  left_join(candidate_asv_table, by = "ASV") %>%
  arrange(p_value)

print(
  asv_spearman_eligible %>%
    select(ASV_ID, rho, p_value, p_adj, n,
           n_source_singles, Family, Genus),
  n = 30
)

top_positive_weight_asvs <- asv_spearman_eligible %>%
  arrange(desc(rho)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20)

top_negative_weight_asvs <- asv_spearman_eligible %>%
  arrange(rho) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20)

print(
  top_positive_weight_asvs %>%
    select(ASV_ID, rho, p_value, p_adj, n, Family, Genus),
  n = 20
)

print(
  top_negative_weight_asvs %>%
    select(ASV_ID, rho, p_value, p_adj, n, Family, Genus),
  n = 20
)

write.csv(
  asv_spearman_eligible,
  "asv_spearman_peso_seco_eligible_samples.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Saved objects:
# asv_spearman_eligible -> eligibility-aware Spearman correlations between ASV abundance and Peso_Seco
# top_positive_weight_asvs -> ASVs most positively associated with Peso_Seco
# top_negative_weight_asvs -> ASVs most negatively associated with Peso_Seco
# Output file:
# asv_spearman_peso_seco_eligible_samples.csv -> full Spearman result table
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# STEP 6 — Residual dry-weight correlations with ASV abundance
#
# Description:
# This chunk tests whether each candidate ASV is associated with
# plant dry weight after removing the mean effect of inoculum
# combination.
#
# First, Peso_Seco is modelled as a function of Componentes.
# The residuals of this model represent whether each plant is heavier
# or lighter than expected for its inoculum combination.
#
# Then, for each candidate ASV, Spearman correlation is calculated
# between ASV relative abundance and residual Peso_Seco, using only
# eligible samples for that ASV.
#
# Output:
# - Eligibility-aware Spearman correlations between ASV abundance
#   and residual plant dry weight
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Calculate residual dry weight after removing Componentes effect
## ------------------------------------------------------------

sample_metadata_resid <- sample_metadata %>%
  filter(!is.na(Peso_Seco)) %>%
  mutate(
    Componentes = factor(Componentes)
  )

peso_model <- lm(Peso_Seco ~ Componentes, data = sample_metadata_resid)

sample_metadata_resid <- sample_metadata_resid %>%
  mutate(
    Peso_Seco_residual = residuals(peso_model)
  )

## Add residuals to ASV long table
asv_long_weight_resid <- asv_long_weight %>%
  select(-any_of("Peso_Seco_residual")) %>%
  left_join(
    sample_metadata_resid %>%
      select(SampleID, Peso_Seco_residual),
    by = "SampleID"
  )

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Spearman correlation per ASV using eligible samples
## ------------------------------------------------------------

candidate_asv_ids <- candidate_asv_table$ASV

asv_spearman_residuals <- lapply(candidate_asv_ids, function(asv_i) {
  
  source_set <- asv_source_sets %>%
    filter(ASV == asv_i) %>%
    pull(source_components) %>%
    .[[1]]
  
  eligible_samples <- sample_info %>%
    filter(
      sapply(Componentes, function(x) {
        any(str_detect(x, source_set))
      })
    )
  
  dat_i <- asv_long_weight_resid %>%
    filter(
      ASV == asv_i,
      SampleID %in% eligible_samples$SampleID,
      !is.na(Peso_Seco_residual)
    )
  
  test_i <- suppressWarnings(
    cor.test(
      dat_i$rel_abundance,
      dat_i$Peso_Seco_residual,
      method = "spearman",
      exact = FALSE
    )
  )
  
  tibble(
    ASV = asv_i,
    n = nrow(dat_i),
    rho_residual = unname(test_i$estimate),
    p_value_residual = test_i$p.value
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj_residual = p.adjust(p_value_residual, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  left_join(candidate_asv_table, by = "ASV") %>%
  arrange(p_value_residual)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Print strongest associations
## ------------------------------------------------------------

print(
  asv_spearman_residuals %>%
    select(ASV_ID, rho_residual, p_value_residual, p_adj_residual,
           n, n_source_singles, Family, Genus),
  n = 30
)

top_positive_weight_asvs_residual <- asv_spearman_residuals %>%
  arrange(desc(rho_residual)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20)

top_negative_weight_asvs_residual <- asv_spearman_residuals %>%
  arrange(rho_residual) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20)

print(
  top_positive_weight_asvs_residual %>%
    select(ASV_ID, rho_residual, p_value_residual,
           p_adj_residual, n, Family, Genus),
  n = 20
)

print(
  top_negative_weight_asvs_residual %>%
    select(ASV_ID, rho_residual, p_value_residual,
           p_adj_residual, n, Family, Genus),
  n = 20
)

write.csv(
  asv_spearman_residuals,
  "asv_spearman_peso_seco_residuals_eligible_samples.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Saved objects:
# peso_model -> linear model removing mean Componentes effect from Peso_Seco
# sample_metadata_resid -> sample metadata with Peso_Seco_residual
# asv_long_weight_resid -> ASV abundance table with residual dry weight
# asv_spearman_residuals -> eligibility-aware correlations between ASV abundance and residual dry weight
# top_positive_weight_asvs_residual -> ASVs most positively associated with residual dry weight
# top_negative_weight_asvs_residual -> ASVs most negatively associated with residual dry weight
# Output file:
# asv_spearman_peso_seco_residuals_eligible_samples.csv -> full residual-correlation result table
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# STEP 7A — Co-occurrence of ASV_106 and ASV_117
#
# Description:
# This chunk determines how often ASV_106 and ASV_117 co-occur
# across samples. ASVs are considered present when relative abundance
# is >= 0.1%.
#
# Samples are classified into four groups:
# - Neither ASV present
# - Only ASV_106 present
# - Only ASV_117 present
# - Both ASVs present
#
# Output:
# - Sample counts per group
# - Mean and median Peso_Seco per group
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

## Get ASV sequences
asv106_seq <- asv_ids %>%
  filter(ASV_ID == "ASV_106") %>%
  pull(ASV)

asv117_seq <- asv_ids %>%
  filter(ASV_ID == "ASV_117") %>%
  pull(ASV)

## Build presence table
asv106_117_presence <- asv_long_weight %>%
  filter(ASV %in% c(asv106_seq, asv117_seq)) %>%
  left_join(asv_ids, by = "ASV") %>%
  mutate(
    present = rel_abundance >= 0.001
  ) %>%
  select(SampleID, Peso_Seco, ASV_ID, present) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = ASV_ID,
    values_from = present
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ASV_106 = ifelse(is.na(ASV_106), FALSE, ASV_106),
    ASV_117 = ifelse(is.na(ASV_117), FALSE, ASV_117),
    group = case_when(
      !ASV_106 & !ASV_117 ~ "Neither",
      ASV_106 & !ASV_117 ~ "ASV_106 only",
      !ASV_106 & ASV_117 ~ "ASV_117 only",
      ASV_106 & ASV_117 ~ "Both"
    )
  )

group_summary <- asv106_117_presence %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_weight = mean(Peso_Seco, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_weight = median(Peso_Seco, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(table(asv106_117_presence$group))
print(group_summary)

# Saved objects:
# asv106_117_presence -> sample-level presence table for ASV_106 and ASV_117
# group_summary -> summary stats per co-occurrence group

# ============================================================
# STEP 7B — Plot Peso_Seco by ASV_106/117 co-occurrence group
#
# Description:
# This chunk visualizes plant dry weight distributions across the
# four ASV co-occurrence groups.
#
# Output:
# - Boxplot + jitter plot of Peso_Seco
# ============================================================

library(ggplot2)

p_asv106_117 <- ggplot(asv106_117_presence,
                       aes(x = group, y = Peso_Seco)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Plant dry weight by ASV_106 / ASV_117 co-occurrence",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Peso_Seco"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

print(p_asv106_117)

ggsave(
  "peso_seco_ASV106_ASV117_groups.png",
  p_asv106_117,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)

# Saved objects:
# p_asv106_117 -> boxplot of Peso_Seco by ASV co-occurrence group
# Output file:
# peso_seco_ASV106_ASV117_groups.png

# ============================================================
# STEP 7C — Formal statistical tests for ASV_106/117 co-occurrence
#
# Description:
# This chunk performs:
# 1. Wilcoxon test comparing "Both" vs all other samples

#
# Output:
# - Wilcoxon p-value
# ============================================================

## Binary variable: both present or not
asv106_117_presence <- asv106_117_presence %>%
  mutate(
    both_present = group == "Both"
  )

## Wilcoxon test
wilcox_both <- wilcox.test(
  Peso_Seco ~ both_present,
  data = asv106_117_presence
)

print(wilcox_both)

asv106_117_presence %>%
  left_join(sample_metadata %>% select(SampleID, Componentes), by = "SampleID") %>%
  filter(group == "Both") %>%
  select(SampleID, Componentes, Peso_Seco)

asv106_117_presence %>%
  left_join(sample_metadata %>% select(SampleID, Componentes), by = "SampleID") %>%
  mutate(has_E = grepl("E", Componentes)) %>%
  filter(has_E) %>%
  group_by(group == "Both") %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_weight = mean(Peso_Seco),
    median_weight = median(Peso_Seco)
  )
# Saved objects:
# wilcox_both -> Wilcoxon test comparing Both vs Rest
```

```{r}
asv106_117_presence %>%
  left_join(
    metadata_centroid %>%
      select(SampleID, distance_to_centroid),
    by = "SampleID"
  ) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),

wilcox.test(
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# STEP 8 — Association between distance to centroid and plant dry weight
#
# Description:
# This chunk evaluates whether plant dry weight is associated with
# the distance of each sample to the global compositional centroid
# (Bray-Curtis attractor).
#
# Three analyses are performed:
# 1. Spearman correlation between distance_to_centroid and Peso_Seco
# 2. Spearman correlation between distance_to_centroid and residual Peso_Seco
# 3. Scatterplot visualization
#
# Output:
# - Correlation statistics
# - Scatterplots with regression lines
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Merge centroid distance with sample metadata
## ------------------------------------------------------------

centroid_weight_df <- metadata_centroid %>%
  select(SampleID, Componentes, distance_to_centroid, Peso_Seco) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Peso_Seco))

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Raw correlation
## ------------------------------------------------------------

cor_centroid_weight <- cor.test(
  centroid_weight_df$distance_to_centroid,
  centroid_weight_df$Peso_Seco,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE
)

print(cor_centroid_weight)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Residual correlation (controlling for Componentes)
## ------------------------------------------------------------

peso_model_centroid <- lm(Peso_Seco ~ Componentes, data = centroid_weight_df)

centroid_weight_df <- centroid_weight_df %>%
  mutate(
    Peso_Seco_residual = residuals(peso_model_centroid)
  )

cor_centroid_weight_resid <- cor.test(
  centroid_weight_df$distance_to_centroid,
  centroid_weight_df$Peso_Seco_residual,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE
)

print(cor_centroid_weight_resid)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Plot raw relationship
## ------------------------------------------------------------

p_centroid_weight <- ggplot(
  centroid_weight_df,
  aes(x = distance_to_centroid, y = Peso_Seco)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Distance to centroid vs plant dry weight",
    x = "Distance to centroid",
    y = "Peso_Seco"
  )

print(p_centroid_weight)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Plot residual relationship
## ------------------------------------------------------------

p_centroid_weight_resid <- ggplot(
  centroid_weight_df,
  aes(x = distance_to_centroid, y = Peso_Seco_residual)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Distance to centroid vs residual plant dry weight",
    x = "Distance to centroid",
    y = "Residual Peso_Seco"
  )

print(p_centroid_weight_resid)

# Saved objects:
# centroid_weight_df -> sample metadata with centroid distance and dry weight
# cor_centroid_weight -> raw correlation test
# cor_centroid_weight_resid -> residual correlation test
# p_centroid_weight -> raw scatterplot
# p_centroid_weight_resid -> residual scatterplot
```
```{r}
# ============================================================
# STEP 9A — Genus-level associations with plant dry weight
#
# Description:
# This chunk collapses ASV abundances at genus level and tests
# whether genus-level relative abundances are associated with
# plant dry weight.
#
# Analyses:
# 1. Raw Spearman correlation with Peso_Seco
# 2. Residual Spearman correlation with residual Peso_Seco
#
# Filtering:
# Genera retained if relative abundance >= 0.1% in at least 10 samples
#
# Output:
# - Significant genera associated with plant dry weight
# ============================================================

library(phyloseq)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Build genus-level abundance table
## ------------------------------------------------------------

otu_mat <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps))
if(taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)

tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("ASV")

tax_df$Genus[is.na(tax_df$Genus)] <- "Unassigned"

otu_long <- as.data.frame(otu_mat) %>%
  rownames_to_column("SampleID") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -SampleID,
    names_to = "ASV",
    values_to = "rel_abundance"
  )

genus_long <- otu_long %>%
  left_join(
    tax_df %>% select(ASV, Genus),
    by = "ASV"
  ) %>%
  group_by(SampleID, Genus) %>%
  summarise(
    rel_abundance = sum(rel_abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    sample_metadata %>% select(SampleID, Peso_Seco),
    by = "SampleID"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    sample_metadata_resid %>% select(SampleID, Peso_Seco_residual),
    by = "SampleID"
  )

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Filter genera
## ------------------------------------------------------------

genus_summary <- genus_long %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(
    n_above_0.1pct = sum(rel_abundance >= 0.001),
    mean_abundance = mean(rel_abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

candidate_genera <- genus_summary %>%
  filter(n_above_0.1pct >= 10) %>%
  pull(Genus)

cat("Number of candidate genera:", length(candidate_genera), "\n")

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Raw Spearman correlations
## ------------------------------------------------------------

genus_spearman <- lapply(candidate_genera, function(g) {
  
  dat <- genus_long %>%
    filter(Genus == g)
  
  test <- cor.test(
    dat$rel_abundance,
    dat$Peso_Seco,
    method = "spearman",
    exact = FALSE
  )
  
  tibble(
    Genus = g,
    rho = unname(test$estimate),
    p_value = test$p.value
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  arrange(p_value)

print(genus_spearman, n = 30)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Residual Spearman correlations
## ------------------------------------------------------------

genus_spearman_resid <- lapply(candidate_genera, function(g) {
  
  dat <- genus_long %>%
    filter(Genus == g)
  
  test <- cor.test(
    dat$rel_abundance,
    dat$Peso_Seco_residual,
    method = "spearman",
    exact = FALSE
  )
  
  tibble(
    Genus = g,
    rho_residual = unname(test$estimate),
    p_value_residual = test$p.value
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj_residual = p.adjust(p_value_residual, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  arrange(p_value_residual)

print(genus_spearman_resid, n = 30)

# Saved objects:
# genus_long
# genus_spearman
# genus_spearman_resid
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# STEP 9B — Family-level associations with plant dry weight
#
# Description:
# This chunk collapses ASV abundances at family level and tests
# whether family-level relative abundances are associated with

#

# Families retained if relative abundance >= 0.1% in at least 10 samples

# - Significant families associated with plant dry weight

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Build family-level abundance table
## ------------------------------------------------------------

tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("ASV")

tax_df$Family[is.na(tax_df$Family)] <- "Unassigned"

family_long <- otu_long %>%
  left_join(
    tax_df %>% select(ASV, Family),
    by = "ASV"
  ) %>%
  group_by(SampleID, Family) %>%
  summarise(
    rel_abundance = sum(rel_abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

    sample_metadata %>% select(SampleID, Peso_Seco),

cat("Number of candidate families:", length(candidate_families), "\n")

## ------------------------------------------------------------

    p_value = test$p.value
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  arrange(p_value)

print(family_spearman, n = 30)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Residual Spearman correlations
## ------------------------------------------------------------

family_spearman_resid <- lapply(candidate_families, function(f) {
  
  dat <- family_long %>%
    filter(Family == f)
  
  test <- cor.test(
    dat$rel_abundance,
    dat$Peso_Seco_residual,
    method = "spearman",
    exact = FALSE
  )
  
  tibble(
    Family = f,
    rho_residual = unname(test$estimate),
    p_value_residual = test$p.value
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj_residual = p.adjust(p_value_residual, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  arrange(p_value_residual)

print(family_spearman_resid, n = 30)
```
